title: Artvin, Şavşat & Borçka Karagöl: Emerald Highland Escape

metaDescription: Reach Borçka Karagöl from Rize-Artvin Airport (RZV), time Şavşat autumn foliage, handle mountain roads with a 4x4 driver, and choose timber lodges.
quickAnswer: Artvin's Borçka Karagöl and Şavşat highlands sit 1.5 to 3.5 hours east of Rize-Artvin Airport (RZV) in northeastern Türkiye. Mid-October to early November brings peak crimson and gold autumn foliage across Şavşat's Cittaslow valleys, while steep gravel plateau tracks and sudden mountain fog make a local 4x4 driver essential.

body.text: Far in Türkiye's northeastern corner, Artvin trades Black Sea coastal sprawl for deep glacial gorges, wooden barns, and landslide lakes ringed by beech and spruce. Because valley roads twist up sheer ridges and weather shifts hourly, planning an Artvin route through [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) focuses on realistic daily driving hours, elevation sequencing, and vetted local drivers rather than packed sightseeing lists.
How do you reach Borçka Karagöl from Rize-Artvin Airport (RZV)?

Borçka Karagöl lies roughly 95 km east of [Rize-Artvin Airport (RZV)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/EN/DefaultEN.aspx), a coastal drive of 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours. Follow the Black Sea D010 coastal highway east to Hopa, turn inland through the Cankurtaran Tunnel to Borçka town, and climb 27 km north along a narrow, forested mountain road to the lake.

The Cankurtaran Tunnel eliminated the old high-pass bottleneck above Hopa, cutting transfer times dramatically from RZV. Once you pass Borçka center, however, the final 27 km ascent to Karagöl Nature Park narrows to two tight lanes with frequent hairpin turns and occasional rockfall after heavy rain. Arriving before 09:30 lets you walk the quiet lakeside loop before day-trip minibuses fill the parking terrace.
Why is autumn foliage in Şavşat considered Türkiye's finest?

Şavşat produces Türkiye's richest autumn color palette because its steep elevation bands—ranging from 900 m valley floors to 2,200 m alpine ridges—stack deciduous beech, maple, oak, and hornbeam directly against dark Caucasian spruce. Designated a member of [Cittaslow Türkiye](https://cittaslowturkiye.org/), the district pairs slow rural architecture with dramatic color shifts from mid-October through early November.

Unlike flat forest parks that turn uniformly yellow, Şavşat's layered microclimates shift week by week. Upper villages such as Maden (Bazgiret) and Yavuzköy ignite in copper and scarlet first, followed by lower valleys around Şavşat Karagöl and the [Go Türkiye 2-day Şavşat route](https://goturkiye.com/routes/2-day-route-savsat). Traditional two-story timber houses (serender grain stores and hand-notched pine chalets) stand directly in the pastures, giving photographers clear foregrounds without power-line clutter or modern concrete resorts.
What mountain road conditions require a local 4x4 driver?

High-clearance 4x4 vehicles with local drivers are necessary beyond paved valley hubs, especially toward Macahel (Camili Biosphere Reserve), Sahara Plateau, Arsiyan Lakes, and upper Şavşat villages. Steep 15% grades, wet clay, loose shale, and thick afternoon fog turn short 25 km highland hops into slow, technical climbs.

Even experienced urban drivers underestimate Artvin's steep switchbacks and narrow passing bays. Passing oncoming logging trucks or village minibuses on a mud-slick ledge requires reversing calmly on blind bends. In Macahel—highlighted as Türkiye's sole UNESCO biosphere reserve on [Go Türkiye's Black Sea Highlands route](https://goturkiye.com/routes/discover-the-black-sea-highlands-in-2-weeks)—the high pass can receive early snow by late October, closing standard two-wheel-drive access overnight.

items: Book flights into Rize-Artvin Airport (RZV) rather than Trabzon (TZX) to save roughly 90 minutes each way.
Carry waterproof hiking boots, thermal mid-layers, and a shell jacket; valley temperatures drop sharply after sunset.
Confirm fuel stops in Hopa, Borçka, or Şavşat before climbing into Macahel or Sahara Plateau.
Keep cash (Turkish lira) on hand for park entry gates, village tea houses, and local chestnut honey.

body.text: Where are the best wooden boutique lodges?

The finest stays in Artvin are small, family-run timber lodges concentrated around Yavuzköy, Veliköy, and Kocabey near Şavşat, plus quiet wooden guesthouses tucked inside the Camili (Macahel) valley. Choose properties built with traditional interlocking pine logs, wood-burning stoves, and valley-facing verandas rather than roadside concrete hotels in Artvin city center.

In Şavşat, wooden bungalow lodges along the Ardahan road and above Yavuzköy place you within 25 to 45 minutes of Şavşat Karagöl while offering home-cooked breakfasts of kuymak (melted cheese and cornmeal), mountain butter, and raw highland honey. Around Borçka, staying in a small riverside timber lodge near Heba or Macahel avoids backtracking to Hopa and lets you wake directly inside the mist-filled valley. For winter mountain trips elsewhere in Türkiye once Artvin's passes close under snow, see our [winter travel guide to Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).

faq.q: How many days are ideal for Borçka Karagöl and Şavşat?
faq.a: Four to five nights is the practical minimum: one night near Borçka or Macahel for Borçka Karagöl, and two to three nights in Şavşat to cover Şavşat Karagöl, Yavuzköy, Maden Village, and Sahara Plateau without rushing mountain drives.

faq.q: Can you visit both Borçka Karagöl and Şavşat Karagöl in one day?
faq.a: Driving between the two lakes takes roughly 3.5 to 4 hours each way via Borçka and Artvin's Çoruh gorge. Visiting both in a single day leaves almost no time on the trails; staying overnight in each valley is far better.

faq.q: When does snow block the high passes in Artvin?
faq.a: Snow routinely dusts passes above 1,800 meters—including the Macahel pass and Sahara Pass—by late October or early November, with full winter closures lasting from December into May.
Yes. Rize-Artvin Airport operates daily domestic flights from Istanbul (IST and SAW) and Ankara year-round, though heavy coastal fog can occasionally delay winter and spring arrivals.

faq.q: Are there restaurants inside Borçka Karagöl Nature Park?
faq.a: A small lakeside café and basic picnic areas operate near the entrance during warmer months, but options are limited off-season. Plan full meals in Borçka town or at your timber lodge.

faq.q: Can you combine Artvin with Kars or Erzurum?
faq.a: Yes. From Şavşat, the scenic Sahara Pass climbs east into Ardahan and continues south to Kars (roughly 3.5 hours in snow-free months), creating a scenic highland circuit from the Black Sea to Eastern Anatolia.
